content: The term FODMAP is an acronym that stands for Fermentable Oligosaccharides, Disaccharides, Monosaccharides, And Polyols. These are short-chain carbohydrates and polyols that are highly fermentable but poorly absorbed in the gastrointestinal tract. A low FODMAP diet has been shown to be potentially beneficial in managing symptoms of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), as supported by evidence from a systematic review of randomized controlled trials and a more recent clinical trial. One of the trials included in the systematic review evaluated the effects of a diet that combined low FODMAP intake with high dietary fiber. A diet that is low in FODMAPs but high in soluble fiber typically includes psyllium, also known as ispaghula husks. A specific high-fiber, low-FODMAP diet has been published, which contains 23 grams of fiber and 3 grams of FODMAPs. It is also worth noting that symptoms attributed to gluten sensitivity in individuals without celiac disease may, in fact, be caused by the presence of fructans in wheat rather than gluten itself.
